readings.title: The bowl with an uneven edge
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: At Copper Lane's craft exhibition, a visitor assumed that an uneven bowl was an unfinished mistake. The maker explained how hand pressure and firing affected its shape, then showed the marks left by each stage. The visitor still preferred a smoother style but understood the work differently. The label did not tell people what they had to admire. It offered information that could make their judgement more informed. A finished object became a starting point for discussing choices, materials and skill rather than simply an item to praise or reject at first glance.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

readings.title: Watching hands instead of slides
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A craft tutor prepared a detailed presentation about basket weaving. Learners understood the vocabulary but struggled to start. She replaced part of the presentation with a close demonstration, pausing at the point where one strip passed behind another. Learners then tried the movement and described what felt difficult. Pictures and notes remained useful reminders, but they could not replace the experience of handling the material. The tutor learnt to choose the medium according to the skill. Knowing the name of a movement was different from being able to perform it.

readings.title: A price tag and an explanation
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A local craft seller often heard that her scarves cost more than factory-made ones. She added a short account of the work involved, including preparation, weaving and finishing. Some visitors continued to choose cheaper products, which she accepted. Others began asking about the process and ordering fewer but longer-lasting items. The explanation was not a demand that everyone share her priorities. It made a hidden part of the price visible. Clear information supported a more informed choice while leaving customers free to decide what fitted their needs and budgets.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

readings.title: The workshop after the exhibition
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A town displayed old woodworking tools but noticed that younger visitors spent little time with them. A retired carpenter offered short supervised sessions using safe demonstration materials. Participants then returned to the display to identify tools related to their experience. The sessions did not make them skilled carpenters, and access to sharp equipment remained controlled. They gave the objects a practical context. Attendance figures mattered, but organisers also listened to the questions visitors asked afterwards. A small experience could create curiosity that a longer written description had not managed to produce.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

translation.stem:
Translate the following original passage into Chinese. Preserve the meaning and logical relationships.

A handmade object carries traces of the choices made by its creator. Explaining those choices can help a visitor see more than a finished product. Traditional skills survive when people have opportunities to practise them. An exhibition can therefore be a place for learning as well as looking.
translation.referenceAnswer: 一件手工制品留下了创作者所作选择的痕迹。解释这些选择，有助于参观者看到成品之外的东西。当人们有机会练习时，传统技艺才能延续。因此，展览既可以是观看的地方，也可以是学习的场所。
translation.explanation: 参考译文仅示范一种表达。评分时关注信息完整性、转折和条件等逻辑关系；意思准确且中文自然的其他译法同样有效。

criteria.description: 准确传达各句核心信息、对象和逻辑关系；按遗漏或误译程度酌情扣分。

criteria.name: 中文表达

writing.stem:
Write an English response of about 120 words to the following original simulation task. Use your own examples and organise your ideas clearly.

Propose an exhibition of local crafts for young visitors. Explain what they could learn and suggest one participatory activity.
writing.sampleAnswer: I propose an exhibition showing how local crafts are made, rather than displaying only finished objects. Young visitors could see the stages of preparing materials, shaping them and adding final details. Short labels should explain choices made by the maker, including why two handmade objects may differ. A supervised weaving activity would let visitors try one simple movement with safe materials. Afterwards, they could compare their work with an experienced maker's example and ask questions. The activity would not aim to produce skilled craftspeople in one afternoon. It would give visitors a practical reason to look more closely at the exhibition. With the makers' agreement, short recordings could also preserve explanations for future visitors.
writing.explanation: 范文供完成作答后对照。允许不同立场与例子；围绕题目要求论述清楚、理由充分、语言准确即可。

criteria.name: 任务完成与内容
criteria.description: 回应题目所有要求，观点明确，包含相关理由、具体例子或可行建议。

criteria.name: 组织与衔接
criteria.description: 结构清楚，信息顺序合理，句段衔接自然，格式符合写作目的。

criteria.name: 语言与表达
criteria.description: 词汇使用恰当，句式基本准确，表达清晰；错误按其对理解的影响扣分。

knowledgePoints: 英语写作：观点、建议与应用文
